thread.title: Apple Stock Falls On Light Sales Guidance For Holiday Quarter | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Falls On Light Sales Guidance For Holiday Quarter | Investor's Business Daily

organizations.name: apple stock falls on light sales guidance

text:
Consumer electronics leader Apple ( AAPL ) late Thursday beat Wall Street's estimates for its fiscal fourth quarter ended Sept. 29. But Apple stock fell in extended trading on the company's lighter-than-expected sales guidance.
X The Cupertino, Calif.-based company earned $2.91 a share on sales of $62.9 billion in the September quarter . Analysts expected it to earn $2.78 a share on sales of $61.57 billion. On a year-over-year basis, earnings per share rose 41% while sales climbed 20%.
Apple guided to sales of $91 billion in the current quarter, missing views. It did not give a target for earnings per share. Wall Street predicted it would earn $4.94 a share on sales of $92.91 billion in the December quarter.
Apple stock sank 4% in after-hours trading on the stock market today . During the regular session, Apple stock rose 1.5% to 222.22.

Apple's fourth-quarter results included just nine days of sales of the company's flagship 12th-generation smartphones, iPhone XS and XS Max. A third model, the iPhone XR, went on sale last Friday.
Services revenue reached an all-time high of $10 billion last quarter, up 27% year over year.
"Over the past two months, we've delivered huge advancements for our customers through new versions of iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad and Mac as well as our four operating systems," Chief Executive Tim Cook said in a news release. "We enter the holiday season with our strongest lineup of products and services ever."
Apple Mulling Deal With iHeartMedia In other news, Apple is exploring a tie-up with iHeartMedia, the largest U.S. radio station operator, to promote its Apple Music streaming service, the Financial Times reported Thursday .
The deal could involve Apple taking an equity stake in the financially struggling iHeartMedia. Or it could result in a multimillion-dollar marketing partnership rather than a direct investment, the report said.
